Impart

im-PART -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, PART. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To impart is to pass on knowledge, wisdom, or skills to someone, like a teacher handing a lesson to a learner.

Grandpa used the long drive north to impart a few hard-won lessons about saving money.

Worked Example

On her last day before retirement, the chemistry teacher sets aside the textbook. 'Forty years of running this lab,' she says, 'taught me three things no manual will tell you' -- and the whole class leans in to write them down.

She is imparting her wisdom: giving specific, valuable knowledge to someone else, often in a formal, teacher-to-learner register. What is imparted is a definite piece of know-how or advice -- handed across like a gift.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

convey: to communicate or make something known

transmit: to pass something along from one person to another

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

withhold: to deliberately keep something back

conceal: to hide something from others

Where it sits · how deliberate and total the sharing is — convey → impart → transmit

convey vs. impart: Convey covers any passing-along of meaning -- a shrug can convey boredom -- while impart is more deliberate and generous: knowledge or wisdom handed over on purpose, usually by someone who has more of it.

transmit vs. impart: Transmit is the strongest about transfer: a signal or a tradition is transmitted whole from point to point, while impart keeps a human teacher in the picture, giving a share of what they know.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: in, to (Latin in-)

root — part-

root — part-: a part, a share (Latin pars, partis)

Put it together

Put it together: Impart comes from Latin impartire, 'to give a share to' -- im- ('to') plus pars ('a part, a share'). To impart wisdom is literally to give someone a share of yours: the knowledge is divided like bread, and afterward you both hold a piece.

Use the root in a new word: particle

Use the root in a new word: particle: A single particle of dust drifted through the beam of the projector.

Word Choice

Impart hands over a specific piece of knowledge, wisdom, or advice: a mentor imparts decades of experience. Keep it apart from its cluster neighbors in this unit -- instill builds a quality of character gradually over time (you instill discipline, not directions), and enlighten corrects ignorance by revealing what someone did not know. Impart gives facts and know-how; instill grows attitudes; enlighten opens eyes.
